To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decays $A\to ZZ, Z \gamma, \gamma \gamma$ are loop-induced in the general 2HDM.
the decays $A^{0} \to Z \gamma, \gamma \gamma, ZZ$ are dominated by fermionic loops and can be used to constrain the 2H2DM.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: - Theoretical analysis of the decays ${ A^0} \leftrightarrow ZZ, \gamma\, \gamma$ and ${A^0}\leftrightarrow Z \, \gamma$ in the framework of the 2HDS, including a general fermionic contribution in the loops.
the search of a heavy pseudoscalar Higgs boson at the LHC, in the context of a general 2HDM.
the following issues: (a) We evaluate the amplitude and branching ratios for the decays $A^{0} \to \gamma \gamma, \gamma Z$ and $ZZ$ in the context of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2-HDM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2HDT is still a viable model for the Higgs sector of new physics.
, if the Higgs spectrum contains a pseudoscalar, it is possible to probe it at the LHC in the decay $A^0\to ZZ$, and in the decay $ A^0 \to Z\gamma$ if $m_{A^0}\lesssim 1$~TeV.

, in a large region of the parameter space, the decay $A^0\to ZZ$ dominates over $A^0{\to}Z\gamma$ and $\gamma\gamma$, which are subdominant, and the branching ratios for $A^ 0\to \gamma\gamma,Z\gamma$ are in the range $\sim (10^{-4} - 10^{-2})$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $A^0$ boson can be detected at the LHC for a wide range of the 2HDP parameters.
the decay modes considered here could be used as complementary channels for the search of $A^0$ in the 2HDP.
the decay $A^0\to \gamma\gamma $ is the most promising decay channel for the pseudoscalar $A^0$ at LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decay ${A^0}\to ZZ$ is the dominant decay for a heavy $A^0$ and it is the best channel for the discovery of a pseudoscalar Higgs boson.
the $A^{0}\to\gamma\gamma$ mode is the only one with a non-negligible branching ratio, and the current experimental limits on the Higgs boson mass exclude the $A^0$ with a mass above 1 TeV.
, even in the absence of a tree-level $A^0$ coupling to $V$, the decay rates of $A^0\to ZZ, Z \gamma, \gamma \gamma$ can be sizable and within the reach of current searches.
